speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) sought views from the public on the draft Bill earlier this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have evaluated the feedback received and incorporated them where they are relevant to the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, these changes ensure parity between local and overseas purchases and will help ease business compliance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes are found in clauses 4 to 9, 15 to 17, 19 and 20 in the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This measure is required for the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore to enforce GST on imported services effectively, as suppliers under the Overseas Vendor Registration regime operate overseas and will need to rely on information provided by customers to determine if GST is applicable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Clause 12 in the Bill provides for these changes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As mentioned earlier, MOF regularly reviews the GST regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I will highlight the last three amendments found in the Bill arising from this periodic review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we will update our GST treatment of digital payment tokens, also commonly known as cryptocurrencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the exchange of fiat currency and the provision of loans in fiat currency are financial services which are exempt from GST.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, the use of fiat currency as payment for goods and services today is not subject to GST.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But increasingly, we are seeing the acceptance of digital payment tokens as a means of payment for goods and services at local retailers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Accordingly, the amendment also seeks to not subject the supply of digital payment tokens to GST, when they are used as a means of payment for goods and services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means that whether digital payment tokens or fiat currency are used to purchase goods and services, GST is chargeable only on the underlying supply of goods and services, not on the digital payment token itself.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This proposed treatment is similar to the GST rules for digital payment tokens in Australia, the European Union, Switzerland and Japan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes that are required to be made to the GST Act are found in clauses 3, 10 and 16 to 18 of the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Clause 11 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Similar changes were passed in this House last month in relation to the Income Tax Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes relating to Court proceedings, under the GST Act and the Income Tax Act, will take effect on 1 January 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Clause 2 of the Bill provides for the change.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These definitions are consistent with those currently found in the Income Tax Act for the purposes of appeals heard before the Income Tax Board of Review.
